parsing.return_type: TABLE(mes_referencia date, total_creditos numeric(18, 2), total_debitos numeric(18, 2), saldo_consolidado numeric(18, 2), qtd_transacoes integer)

risks.message: Recursive CTE should stay in SQL; re-implementing it in Python is costly.
Depends on other database routines: fn_saldo_cliente.

recommendations.message: Keep joins, aggregates, CTEs and bulk DML as parameterized SQL.
Map RAISE EXCEPTION to typed exceptions and RAISE NOTICE to logging.
Return OUT/INOUT parameters as an immutable result type.
Return RETURN QUERY rows as a sequence of typed rows.

architectural_decisions.decision: The recursive CTE (months chain), the aggregated subquery over transacoes/contas and the final LEFT JOIN remain as one parameterized query executed via sqlalchemy.text().
architectural_decisions.rationale: Joins, aggregates and recursive CTEs belong in the database; reimplementing recursion/aggregation in Python would be slower and less faithful.

architectural_decisions.decision: fn_saldo_cliente is still called inside the database via SELECT fn_saldo_cliente(:cliente_id); its scalar result is bound as :v_saldo_atual into the main query.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Its implementation was not provided, so translating it would risk behavioural drift; keeping it server-side preserves exact semantics.

warnings: RAISE EXCEPTION became PeriodoInvalidoError raised before any SQL executes; callers relying on catching generic SQLSTATE errors must adapt.

Original WHEN OTHERS caught every error including those raised by fn_saldo_cliente; here the initial period check raises outside the try-block intentionally (it maps to RAISE EXCEPTION, which propagated anyway). All other failures fall back to the degraded row like the original.

If the fallback SELECT itself fails (e.g., broken connection), the exception propagates instead of returning a row — impossible-to-reproduce edge case of the original where the fallback could also fail silently.
saldo_consolidado can be Decimal|None because v_saldo_atual comes from fn_saldo_cliente whose nullability is unknown; the original coerced NULL implicitly at output time.
Assumes fn_saldo_cliente exists in the target database; verify before deployment.
No row locks needed (read-only routine); transaction ownership left entirely to the caller.
